report: # Heat tolerance of a soil lipase
We heated the purified enzyme at 50, 60 and 70 °C and measured the residual activity. The enzyme kept 74 % of its activity after one hour at 60 °C.
The enzyme was incubated at 37 °C for 30 min before each assay. Samples were taken every 10 min, and the residual activity was recieved as the mean of three replicates.
A pilot study with 18 samples was run in March to test the assay and is not part of the results.
The half-life of the enzyme at 60 °C was 42 min, and the difference between the two buffers was significant (p = 0.02).
At 70 °C the color of the reaction mixture changed from yellow to clear within 15 min.
The enzyme is stable enough for detergents that are used at 60 °C, but its half-life at 70 °C is too short for industrial use.
terms: The sorbent was washed with water and dried at 105 °C.
We weighed 0.2 g of the sorbent into each flask.
After 24 h the sorbent was filtered off and the solution was analysed.
The capacity of the sorbent was 1.85 mmol/g.
ru: Цеолит промывали водой и сушили при 105 °C. Навеску 0,2 г встряхивали со 100 мл раствора в течение 24 ч.
Сорбент отделяли фильтрованием, концентрацию меди в растворе определяли атомно-абсорбционным методом.
Ёмкость модифицированного сорбента составила 1,85 ммоль/г, природного — 0,92 ммоль/г. Сорбент сохранял ёмкость после пяти циклов регенерации.
ru-dash: Ёмкость модифицированного сорбента - 1,85 ммоль/г, природного - 0,92 ммоль/г. Цеолит - доступный и недорогой сорбент.

copy: The residual activity of the purified lipase was measured after incubation at 50, 60 and 70 °C in 50 mM phosphate buffer at pH 7.5, using p-nitrophenyl butyrate as the substrate, with three technical replicates per temperature, and the values were normalised to the activity of an unheated control sample that was kept on ice for the whole duration of the experiment.
The enzyme kept 74 % of its activity after one hour at 60 °C.
claim: Lipases remove fatty stains from fabrics at low washing temperatures.
Lipases are the second most widely used enzymes in household detergents after proteases.
Most detergent lipases are produced in fungi and expressed in yeast.
spin: Membrane transporters change shape when they bind a substrate, and these changes are hard to follow in a lipid bilayer.

Three methods can follow such changes: calorimetry measures the heat of binding but not the structure, fluorescence reports distances only with bulky dyes, and spin labelling gives distances of 2–8 nm with small probes.
Here we combine spin labelling with molecular dynamics to follow one transporter through its transport cycle.
The protein was labelled at two cysteines and reconstituted into liposomes.
Distances were measured at 50 K with a four-pulse sequence.

The mean distance grew from 3.1 nm to 4.2 nm when the substrate was added. The distance distribution also became broader, which usually points to a mobile loop. Both changes reversed after the substrate was washed out.
spin-ratios: The protein was labelled at two cysteines and reconstituted into liposomes.
The mean ratio of the two distance peaks was 0.47 in the control and 1.10 after the substrate was added.

The samples were frozen in liquid nitrogen within one minute.
Spectra were recorded at 50 K with a four-pulse sequence.
